items.title: IMO launches survey on Maritime Single Windows
points: The IMO has launched a survey with the view to gathering information on the level of implementation and use of Maritime Single Window (MSW) systems to better understand the impact of MSW implementation on the administrative workload of maritime…

Maritime Single Windows (MSW) are a means of reducing a ship’s reporting burden by enabling information required for a port call to be exchanged once, digitally and efficiently, using harmonised data standards that allow different authorities and systems…
However, there is a need to test whether MSWs are actually delivering the benefits they were introduced to achieve.

items.title: Karnataka reports ethanol concentration in petrol up to 31.2%
points: Petrol sold in seven Karnataka districts contained ethanol concentrations as high as 31.2%, with eleven of 14 samples exceeding the 20% blend specified under the E20 standard, according to the state government.
The government said the highest concentration was recorded in a sample collected from an Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) outlet, containing 31.2% ethanol.
A sample of Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL)’s Power petrol had 30.5%, while another sample from the company recorded 27% and a BPCL Speed sample contained 26.5%, it added.
The laboratory certificates attached to the statement record the ethanol concentrations in the samples, including 31.2% in an IOCL sample and 30.5% in an HPCL Power sample.
The government said even vehicles sold after April 2023 are certified for ethanol blends of up to 20%.
That calculation assumes a 10% reduction in mileage, annual petrol consumption of 6,200 crore litres and a price of ₹100 a litre.

points: It found that students taught by reservation-category faculty performed marginally better in their immediate course examinations, scoring an average of 1.44 percentile points higher.

The data were collected in two phases — October to December 2017 and January to March 2019 — as part of a larger project funded by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), India’s technical education regulator.
